fact: ANTIM states that SNISI integrates the tools of separate NGO-funded collection systems (nutrition, blindness, reproductive health, malaria, community mortality) into one common database with unified data transmission, a single user directory and unified access to each project's data, and says it allows cross-project analysis; no figures given.

The abstract says community health worker smartphone data on births and perinatal deaths (729 live births and 35 perinatal deaths in eight months, four districts) were analysed on DHIS2 and that the DISK-Mali tool is integrated into the DHIS2 platform.
A DGSHP deputy director is quoted as saying interoperability between DHIS2 and DISC-Mali had been established, in a Muso article on a workshop of 30-31 July 2025; no volumes given.

Muso and DGSHP held a workshop on 30-31 July 2025 to harmonise indicators and plan the integration of Muso's community health toolkit data into DHIS2, described as a first step with further sessions planned including in Koulikoro.
